description: Understand the fundamentals of reinforcement learning. Model sequential decision-making problems using Markov Decision Processes. Design and analyze value-based and policy-based reinforcement learning algorithms. Apply temporal difference learning methods. Implement Monte Carlo and Dynamic Programming algorithms. Develop reinforcement learning solutions for real-world applications. Understand advanced reinforcement learning methods including function approximation and policy gradients.

syllabus.title: Introduction to Reinforcement Learning
syllabus.body: Learning paradigms, elements of RL, agent-environment interaction, rewards and returns, policies, value functions, exploration vs. exploitation; multi-armed bandit problem, action-value methods, incremental implementation, Upper Confidence Bound (UCB), gradient bandit algorithms.

syllabus.title: Markov Decision Processes and Dynamic Programming
syllabus.body: Markov property, Markov reward processes, Markov Decision Processes, Bellman equations, optimal value functions, policy evaluation, policy improvement, policy iteration, value iteration, generalized policy iteration, asynchronous dynamic programming.

syllabus.title: Monte Carlo and Temporal Difference Learning
syllabus.body: Monte Carlo prediction and control, exploring starts, on-policy and off-policy prediction, importance sampling; temporal difference learning: TD(0), SARSA, expected SARSA, Q-learning, double Q-learning, maximization bias.

syllabus.title: n-Step Methods, Eligibility Traces and Planning
syllabus.body: n-step prediction, n-step SARSA, tree backup, eligibility traces, TD(λ), SARSA(λ), forward and backward views; planning and learning, Dyna-Q, prioritized sweeping.

syllabus.title: Function Approximation and Advanced Reinforcement Learning
syllabus.body: Approximate value functions, linear function approximation, gradient descent methods, semi-gradient TD, neural network approximation; policy gradient methods: policy parameterization, REINFORCE algorithm, actor-critic architecture.

outcomes: Explain the reinforcement learning framework and formulate RL problems.
Apply Dynamic Programming and Monte Carlo methods for solving MDPs.
Implement Temporal Difference learning algorithms including SARSA and Q-learning.
Develop reinforcement learning models using function approximation and deep neural networks.
Evaluate advanced reinforcement learning algorithms for practical applications.
textbooks: Richard S. Sutton, Andrew G. Barto, Francis Bach, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd Edition, MIT Press, 2018.
Csaba Szepesvari, Algorithms for Reinforcement Learning, Morgan and Claypool, 2010.
referenceBooks: Maxim Lapan, Deep Reinforcement Learning Hands-On.
Phil Winder, Reinforcement Learning: Industrial Applications of Intelligent Agents, O'Reilly Media, 2020.
